So, here's my little EPA story.

Near Cleveland, OH there's a place called the West Creek Reservation. It's a multi-million dollar park dedicated to keeping our rivers and streams clean.

My friend loves hiking - so she signed up for a program where you get recognition if you hike every trail in every Cleveland MetroPark.

Well, she's a little... detail oriented. One day she stopped and looked down in the rocks of a stream beneath one of the bridges on one of the paths. Know what she saw?

Strange jagged shapes... non-natural shapes... Something just didn't seem right to her, so she hiked down to take a closer look and found that the stream bed was filled with shards of broken glass and porcelain - even metal. All kinds of random debris.

Even stranger, most of it had markings from US Government Hospitals of all things.

So... she figured it all washed down stream from somewhere, so she investigated. What she found was so shocking - she decided to show me first-hand.

As a light drizzle fell, she brought her husband and me out to the bridge and asked me what I saw. After a while I saw it. "Broken glass?!?"

Then motioned for me to follow her... we walked up the creek bed - careful not to step on any of the shards of broken medical containers - and obvious hospital debris (most of it metallic).

Finally, standing in a light rain storm, we rounded a bend and there it was... A wall of garbage about a story and a half high - all kids of broken glass, pottery, and medical junk. It was the side of an old US Government Hospital's medical waste dump. Over the years, the stream had eroded the side of the landfill causing it to spill it's revolting guts into a stream that flows into a park dedicated to demonstrating how we ca preserve clean water.

Media wouldn't cover it. Ohio EPA said they were over-worked and couldn't touch it because it was Federal. Federal EPA wouldn't comment.

So... there it sits today. Government Medical Waste dumping broken glass (and who knows what else) into a creek in a public park dedicated to clean water.
